newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ expresses shock at killing of nurse in Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: NZ expresses shock at killing of nurse in Chechnya.

text.p: New Zealand Foreign Minister Don McKinnon said on Wednesday he was shocked to learn of the "execution" of a New Zealand nurse in Chechnya, one of six Red Cross aid workers killed on Tuesday.
"I was shocked to learn of the cold-blooded execution of Ms (Sheryl) Thayer and her colleagues," McKinnon said in a statement.
"This is serious set-back to the cause of humanitarian aid."

Masked gunmen stormed into an International Committee of the Red Cross compound in Novye Atagi village just southwest of Chechnya's capital Grozny at dawn and shot dead six Western staff, five of them women, as they slept.
The killings spurred several international relief organisations to pull out of Chechnya.
McKinnon said he was calling on his ambassador in Moscow to report back to Wellington as soon as possible.
"The New Zealand government trusts that the perpetrators will be found and brought to justice," he said.
He called on all parties to respect the Chechnya peace settlement.

"I do not know what impact this tragedy will have on the settlement, but we call on all parties to respect the settlement and above all continue to afford the protection that is owed to those courageous aid workers," McKinnon said.
Wellington hospital cancelled all elective surgery as staff were so upset at the news of Thayer's death.
The 40 year-old nurse only stopped work at the hospital three weeks ago and had been in Chechnya just two weeks.
"Quite a number of the staff are in an advanced state of shock and considerable distress and they have been offered grief counselling this morning," a hospital spokesman said.
